newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent and gas oil lose ground on weaker NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent and gas oil lose ground on weaker NYMEX.

text.p: IPE Brent and gas oil futures slipped back on Thursday after NYMEX crude and heating oil futures opened weaker on continued profit-taking after the week's earlier spike, brokers said.

October Brent futures were trading down 21 cents at $21.90 per barrel by 1440 GMT, while September gas oil stood at $208.25 per tonne, up 75 cents on Wednesday's close, but off an intra-day high of $209.00.
"Trade selling is coming into NYMEX," one broker said.
Brokers said they expected both IPE crude and gas oil futures to continue to consolidate, but that the market was still nervous about tension in the Middle East.
"Look for consolidation in a nervous, headline-driven market," said Prudential-Bache in a note to clients.

Analyst said Energy Information Administration figures released on Thursday were in line with expectations and Wednesday's American Petroleum Institute data. The EIA said U.S. crude stocks fell five million barrels from the previous week and brokers said this could provide for October crude.
U.S. gasoline stocks were down 3.4 million barrels, while U.S. distillate stocks were up 3.5 million barrels.
Brokers said the rise in distillates was bearish for heating oil, but some noted that stocks were still 18 million barrels below a year ago.
With Hurricane Fran off the coast off the South Carolina, brokers said the market would be keeping an eye on the weather as an indicator of coming winter demand.
